claims.text: Approximately 75% cold rolling followed by short aging near 350 °C for 15 minutes will simultaneously improve mechanical durability, room-temperature creep resistance, and corrosion resistance relative to the solution-treated state.
The solution-treated Ti–Nb–Mo–Sn example alloy has a predominantly single-phase structure.
Cold rolling substantially refines the beta-phase grain structure.
Severe cold rolling increases the alloy's dislocation density.
Aging near 350 °C for 15 minutes triggers formation of an alpha-containing secondary phase.
The aging step produces fine and evenly dispersed precipitates after 75% cold rolling.
Ultrafine grains and precipitate strengthening impede dislocation motion and thereby increase yield strength and mechanical durability.
Dislocation pinning by fine precipitates reduces the room-temperature creep rate.
Ultrafine grains and fine precipitates promote a more uniform and stable protective passive oxide film.
Improved passive-film uniformity and stability increase corrosion resistance.
The treated alloy will have a lower room-temperature creep rate than the solution-treated baseline.
The treated alloy will exhibit higher polarization resistance and lower corrosion current density than the solution-treated baseline.
The solution-treated baseline has a coarser grain structure than the heavily cold-rolled state.
The solution-treated baseline has lower dislocation and precipitate densities than the treated state.
The predicted simultaneous improvement should hold at room temperature under moderate saline exposure representative of aerospace-fastener service.
Excessive precipitate coarsening or substantially different temperature or chemical conditions may reduce the treatment benefit.
In Ti80–Nb10–Mo5–Sn5, 75% cold rolling significantly increases yield strength.
Cold rolling and precipitation-hardening treatments increase the corrosion resistance of Ti80–Nb10–Mo5–Sn5.
The quantitative room-temperature creep improvement and optimal processing parameters for the intended fastener alloy remain undetermined.
Nanoindentation provides a small-scale, relatively short-duration method for assessing creep behavior.
